This list starts at 8 and flows across pages without explicit breaks. The outer marker visibly widens from 9
to 10, and item 10 contains a lower-alpha nested sequence. Every parent and child has unique start and
end markers so missing, duplicated, or misplaced continuation text is immediately visible.

8. PARENT 08 START — Verify the intake record, the responsible reviewer, the effective date, and
the supporting evidence before advancing the request to the next stage. — PARENT 08 END.
• CHILD 08A START — Confirm that every source identifier remains readable after wrapping
and that the continuation aligns beneath Confirm rather than beneath the bullet marker. —
CHILD 08A END.
• CHILD 08B START — Record unresolved questions in ordinary language so a later reader
can understand both the decision and the exact evidence still required. — CHILD 08B END.
9. PARENT 09 START — Compare the proposed change with the current policy and keep the
explanation long enough to wrap naturally without adding manual line or page breaks. —
PARENT 09 END.
• CHILD 09A START — Preserve the first-line hanging indent when this sentence wraps
through several clauses about ownership, timing, review, and approval. — CHILD 09A END.
• CHILD 09B START — Keep this sibling marker aligned with CHILD 09A even though the
visible prose has a different length and reaches a different final word. — CHILD 09B END.
10. PARENT 10 START — Assess the operational impact, identify reversible steps, and distinguish
immediate safeguards from improvements that can wait for the next release. — PARENT 10
END.
a. CHILD 10A START — A page boundary may occur within this region, but source order, bullet
ownership, and wrapped indentation must remain unchanged on both sides of that boundary.
— CHILD 10A END.
b. CHILD 10B START — No backend may repeat the marker, omit the final phrase, or reset the
surrounding ordered sequence merely because pagination interrupted the nested list. —
CHILD 10B END.
11. PARENT 11 START — Summarize the review outcome with enough context for someone who
did not attend the meeting and cannot infer meaning from a short status code alone. — PARENT
11 END.
• CHILD 11A START — W rapped lines should begin at a stable text position that is deeper
than the parent text and visibly separate from the nested bullet. — CHILD 11A END.
• CHILD 11B START — The final line of this child remains part of the same item even when it
is short, and the following parent must return to the outer indentation level. — CHILD 11B
END.
FLOW END — outer markers 8 through 11, nested lower-alpha markers a and b under item 10, and the
other six nested bullets appear once in source order with stable hanging indents and natural page flow.
